title: Broadcom Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC at Hot Chips 2026
gist: At Hot Chips 2026 Broadcom detailed Thor Ultra, its 800GbE Ethernet NIC for AI/HPC fabrics: a 5nm, 2.4B-transistor chip with PCIe Gen6, enhanced RoCE (packet spraying, out-of-order placement, selective ACK), and programmable congestion control, posting ~97-99% of line rate in TCP and RDMA benchmarks. The launch puts Broadcom in direct 800G NIC competition with NVIDIA's ConnectX-8 and AMD's Vulcano.

insights.claim: Broadcom's Thor Ultra launch places the company directly in the 800G AI-fabric NIC contest against NVIDIA's ConnectX-8 and AMD's Vulcano, extending Broadcom's Ethernet-for-AI systems play beyond switches into endpoint silicon.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: AI networking endpoints are now a three-way merchant-silicon fight; watch NIC share shifts as a leading indicator for Broadcom vs NVIDIA networking revenue.
insights.quote: This Thor Ultra launch puts Broadcom squarely in the 800G NIC contest alongside NVIDIA’s ConnectX-8 and AMD’s Vulcano.

insights.claim: Broadcom is positioning Ethernet as the unified fabric across scale-up (in rack), scale-out (across racks), and scale-across (between data centers) for AI/HPC, a framing that sits awkwardly against NVIDIA's competing framework presented in the same Hot Chips session block.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Ethernet-everywhere vs NVIDIA's proprietary-plus-Ethernet stack is the core standards battle determining who captures AI networking spend.
insights.quote: It is a little bit awkward given what NVIDIA’s framewrok will look like later in this session block.
insights.locator: Broadcom is setting the stage for Thor Ultra

insights.claim: Thor Ultra hardware (cards and chip) was already shown nearly a year earlier at OCP Summit 2025, indicating the product is well past paper-launch stage with Hot Chips 2026 adding architectural depth rather than announcing new silicon.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Suggests Thor Ultra is at or near shipping maturity; revenue contribution timing is nearer-term than a fresh announcement would imply.
insights.quote: Given we saw the physical cards and chip almost a year ago at OCP Summit 2025, it was cool to get more detail on the parts.
insights.locator: Broadcom Thor Ultra 800GbE OCP NIC 3.0 Adapter

insights.claim: Broadcom's Thor Ultra is a 5nm, 2.4-billion-transistor NIC in a 27x27 package drawing 40-42W max at the chip level (50-55W board without optics), pairing a PCIe Gen6 x16 host interface with 8x100G Serdes, 256 SR-IOV virtual functions, and offloads for RoCEv2, stateless packet processing, and inline encryption.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: PCIe Gen6 support and sub-55W power position Thor Ultra for next-gen GPU servers where NIC power and host bandwidth are binding constraints.

insights.claim: Thor Ultra ships in OCP NIC 3.0 and PCIe form factors where a single OSFP112 port can run as 800G, 2x400G, 4x200G, or 8x100G, letting operators reuse one board across multiple port densities and cabling types (DAC, LPO, AEC, optics).
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Port flexibility lowers SKU count and eases hyperscaler qualification, a practical adoption lever versus rivals; LPO support ties into the low-power optics trend.

themes.theme: Enhanced RoCE and Congestion Control Architecture

insights.claim: Thor Ultra's generational leap over the prior Thor centers on packet spraying with out-of-order placement across up to eight planes, reliability beyond Go-Back-N via selective ACK/NACK retransmission, programmable congestion control, and double the ports with multiplane connectivity.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: These are exactly the Ultra Ethernet-style features needed to make Ethernet competitive with InfiniBand for AI collectives; validates the Ethernet-for-AI thesis.
insights.quote: packet spraying with out-of-order placement, reliability beyond Go-Back-N, simpler, programmable congestion control, and double the ports with multiplane connectivity
insights.locator: Thor Ultra Ethernet NIC – Generational Context

insights.claim: Thor Ultra's congestion control baseline is Receiver Credit-Based Congestion Control, where the receiver hands credits to active senders and uses speculative credits for line-rate startup, with P4-like match-action engines allowing operators to customize the algorithm and awareness of ECN, trimming, and CSIG telemetry.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Programmable congestion control lets hyperscalers tune fabrics to their own workloads, a stickiness and differentiation vector versus fixed-function NICs.
insights.locator: Congestion control centers on Receiver Credit-Based

insights.claim: For GPU/XPU systems, Thor Ultra uses upstream dma-buf for local peer-to-peer DMA between NIC and GPU memory and eRoCE for remote transfers, connecting to NCCL, RCCL, and MPI via a verbs provider and xCCL plugins so applications run unmodified.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: An upstream, unmodified-application software path reduces switching costs away from NVIDIA's networking stack, key to actual deployment wins.
insights.quote: an upstream dma-buf peer memory model that leaves applications unmodified

insights.claim: Broadcom identifies multipathing, RoCE reliability/out-of-order enhancements, and programmable congestion control as the hard engineering problems of this generation, all tracing back to the packet processing pipeline design.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Pipeline architecture is the moat claim; competitors bolting these features onto older pipelines may lag on efficiency.

insights.claim: On a two-node Gen5 GPU platform (8 GPUs per node, 16 ranks over sixteen 400G links), Thor Ultra delivered 383.93 GB/s all_reduce and 380.23 GB/s reduce_scatter against a 400 GB/s ceiling, with bus bandwidth above 96% of line rate across most collectives; alltoall was the outlier at 84.62 GB/s.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: >96% collective efficiency on Ethernet undercuts the InfiniBand performance argument; watch whether independent tests confirm vendor numbers.
insights.quote: Bus bandwidth holds above 96% of line rate across most operations.

insights.claim: Thor Ultra TCP throughput via iperf3 on a Gen6 CPU with 512 GB DDR5-8000 reached 791 Gbps unidirectional at 16 flows (~98.9% of 800G) and roughly 1.51 Tbps bidirectional, saturating near-linearly by eight flows.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Near-line-rate TCP at 800G shows the part is not RDMA-only; broad workload applicability widens the addressable market.

insights.claim: RDMA writes on Thor Ultra saturate at 781 Gbps unidirectional and 1558 Gbps bidirectional (~97.6% of the 1.6 Tb/s aggregate), hitting about 88% of line rate by 32 KB message sizes and within 3% of peak by 128 KB.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Strong small-to-mid message-size efficiency matters for AI collective traffic patterns; this is the spec buyers will benchmark against ConnectX-8.
insights.locator: Thor Ultra Throughput for RDMA Writes

insights.claim: Thor Ultra embeds silicon-level security (FUSE-based root of trust, ROM bootstrap, authenticated firmware, SPDM attestation, PSP encryption) plus PTPv2 nanosecond timestamping and PTM timing, targeting multi-tenant XPU-as-a-service and CPU-as-a-service deployments rather than just raw bandwidth.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Security/timing/manageability features signal Broadcom is courting neocloud and hyperscaler rental businesses, not just internal training clusters.
insights.quote: QoS plus virtualization enable XPU and CPU as a service, with security, manageability, and timing for sync across systems

insights.claim: Broadcom's Linux stack for Thor Ultra (bng_re RoCE driver, bng_en NIC driver, libbng_re library) rides standard libibverbs and rdma-core interfaces, keeping the software path open-standards-based rather than proprietary.
insights.speaker: Patrick Kennedy
insights.so_what: Standards-based drivers ease multi-vendor fabric strategies, reinforcing the anti-lock-in pitch hyperscalers want.
insights.locator: RoCE Software Components for Linux OS
